execution.isolation: Give a fresh context one raw input and the runtime skill path. Hide other cases and the rubric.
execution.permissions: Allow skill resource reads. Prohibit network, product or helper execution, Git, credentials, and delegation. Only the saved-report case may write its report inside one fresh system temporary directory.
execution.assessment: Assess the actual result semantically. Supplied facts and proposed checks do not imply new execution.

cases.input: Use exactly Baseline, Impact, and Evidence in chat. REQ-17 adds a unique index on customer.email for a new import. Our planning snapshot a1 describes customer.email and a shared design note says email remains required. The current integration revision b2 contains a merged migration renaming email to contact_email. The import runs under old and new writers during rollout, and we have not measured duplicates or verified either writer at b2. No production status is available. Review this proposed change without editing files. Identify what can proceed, what depends on a decision, and what needs verifying.
expected: Use exactly the requested sections and distinguish the two revisions, the shared invariant, and production state.
Identify the invalidated index target. Assess the change using current column semantics, existing duplicates, and compatibility of supported writers.
Name concrete checks for the combined candidate and a populated upgrade. State that these checks are pending.
prohibited: Use the stale column as if it still exists or approve migration readiness without evidence
Claim deployment, test results, or authority to edit shared assets
cases.quality: The review explains what would fail and what evidence would support a compatible revision of the plan.

cases.input: Propose a full standalone data impact report in chat. At integrated revision a17, profiles and subscriptions are planned but no users table exists. The approved initial design describes users with a unique stable internal ID and one profile per user. A separate pending change Identity owns creation of users but has neither merged nor produced a migration file. REQ-3 requires creating a profile only for an existing user, enforcing at most one profile per user, and rejecting writes to profiles owned by another tenant. Tenant scope ownership and the allowed behavior when a user is deleted are unspecified. Both profiles and subscriptions need users. We have no environment or test results and no file changes are requested.
expected: Use the standalone report structure and distinguish the approved design from integrated schema.
Assign creation to Identity once. Make both features depend on the integrated prerequisite and express the profile change conditionally.
Leave tenant ownership and deletion semantics unresolved. Specify relevant existence, uniqueness, concurrency, and tenant-isolation checks.
prohibited: Duplicate creation, claim a migration file exists, or invent a cascade or tenant ownership rule
Treat approval of intent or a pending change as completed schema work
cases.quality: The report preserves supported analysis while naming the exact decisions and evidence needed before dependent implementation.

cases.input: Analyze only REQ-8: a signed-in tenant operator may list the latest order events for their own tenant. Snapshot s23 shows an existing API-independent persistent read path in the owned document store and a matching compound index on tenantId and descending occurredAt. The UI derives a display label from the existing event type without persisting it. No new writes, retention rules, schema changes or test results were supplied. Give a brief focused impact assessment in chat.
expected: Use the supplied baseline, preserve REQ-8, and explain the existing read path and index fit.
Keep tenant isolation and derived display values explicit. Give focused verification without inventing a model change.
prohibited: Require a full report, new migration, or persisted UI label
Claim an executed query plan or test result
cases.quality: The output remains brief while identifying the behavior and existing-data boundaries that still need checking.

cases.input: Write a full standalone data-impact report in English in a fresh isolated temporary directory. There is no naming or layout convention for this fixture. For REQ-22, subscriptions with existing status paused must be excluded from renewal processing. At baseline r41 a persisted subscriptions.status already allows paused and active. Every record has a status, and the existing worker's read path and index already support filtering by it. There are no changes to schema, stored records, or the write path. During deployment, any old worker can still renew paused subscriptions, so deployment must replace or drain all old workers before enabling the new behavior. The separate deployment owner has not selected the mechanism. Describe the rollout and verification needs without running the application or database, then report the saved path.
expected: Save and read back a UTF-8 data-impact.md in the temporary directory. Use the full standalone template and remove prompts and comments.
Preserve REQ-22 and r41. Include coordinated rollout because old workers can violate the new behavior. Leave the choice of mechanism with the deployment owner.
Describe verification of active and paused processing and retirement of old workers. Distinguish planned checks from file verification.
prohibited: Invent a migration, schema change, deployment mechanism, or executed product result
cases.quality: The delivered file is independently useful and describes an actionable rollout dependency even though the schema is stable.
